clue.text: Uncle's place where poor shown to invest in rubbish

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the scrambled word goes inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: pap is worthless or trivial material, rubbish

indicators.note: poor signals that the word shown is in bad shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A down-and-out is put on display among the junk at a relative's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so the definition is the pawnbroker's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, whose place of business is a pawnbroker's shop.

clue.text: Lancashire city not entirely quick

indicators.note: not entirely means the city's name is given short of its final letter

parts.note: Preston is a city in Lancashire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A northern English city is described as only partly fast-paced.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON is a city in Lancashire, in north-west England; 'not entirely' drops its last letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical tempo marking meaning very fast, so it serves as a synonym for quick.

clue.text: Far off with wet bird? Certainly not!

definitions.text: Far off with wet bird? Certainly not!

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of far and wet go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bird is soaked and distant, and is firmly told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the hint: a duck's oiled feathers keep it dry, so is a waterbird wet? Certainly not!
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks, geese and swans are birds of the water whose oily plumage sheds wet, so they never get soaked.

clue.text: Bloomer followed up two thousand years ago?

definitions.meaning: a bloomer is a flowering plant, here a bulb with white starry flowers

definitions.text: followed up two thousand years ago?
definitions.meaning: the wise men followed a light in the sky at the Nativity, looking up as they went

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a white-flowered bulb and to the guiding light the Magi followed to the Nativity.

clue.text: North American city where kind of train carried by wheels?

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the scrambled word sits between the two wheels

parts.note: wheels are round, like two letter O shapes

indicators.note: kind of signals a variant form of the word train, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller asks which city in America has a special locomotive running on wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: Ontario is better known as a Canadian province, but a city in California shares the name; 'wheels' gives two round O shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a city in southern California, as well as the Canadian province, so it fits a North American city.

clue.text: Anger when sleep disturbed before noon

indicators.note: before places the scrambled word ahead of the single letter
disturbed signals that the word sleep is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone woken from a nap before midday gets cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means bad temper or irritable rage, the spleen once being held to be the seat of ill humour.

clue.text: Drink about gallon, sum drunk includes last of scotch, pub fare

indicators.note: about means around, so the drink's letters wrap the scrambled group

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink

indicators.note: drunk signals that the words gallon and sum are reeling, their letters rearranged
last of means the final letter of the word scotch is taken

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink, adds up a tab, and gets merry on whisky over a meal at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes H from scotch; 'includes' adds it to GALLON and SUM, and 'drunk' scrambles all ten into LOUGHMANSL. 'about' wraps PUNCH round them. A ploughman's lunch is bread, cheese and pickle, a British pub staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploughman's lunch, bread with cheese and pickle, is a classic cold dish served in British pubs.

clue.text: Record time claimed by Frenchman on the up

indicators.note: on the up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse
claimed by means taken inside, so the time letter goes within the name

parts.note: Rene is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman on his way up takes credit for a time on the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claimed by' puts T inside RENE to give RETNE, and 'on the up' reads that upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to record them, as in entering a figure in a ledger.

clue.text: Explosive gas, as invisible, no inert gas

indicators.note: explosive signals that the letters blow apart and are rearranged
as invisible means the letters a and s vanish from the word gas

explanation.surface: A chemist describes a dangerous gas that cannot be seen and is not inert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invisible' takes AS out of the second gas, leaving G; 'Explosive' scrambles NO, INERT and G. 'Explosive gas' reads as one phrase, but Explosive is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a chemical element that exists as a colourless gas making up most of the air.

clue.text: Way up (or high state)

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bracketed aside notes that a road climbs, or perhaps someone is stoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, senseless condition, such as a drug-induced high may bring on.

clue.text: More old pictures sent back

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: sent back means the word for pictures is read in reverse

parts.note: art is paintings and pictures

explanation.surface: A gallery returns more antique paintings than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, beyond the usual amount, so it serves as a synonym for more.

clue.text: Keep at going after bird, giving as good as you get

definitions.text: giving as good as you get

indicators.note: going after places the keep and at behind the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort

explanation.surface: Someone retaliates against a bird that pecks at them, going after it.
explanation.walkthrough: A keep is the central tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tit for tat means retaliating in kind, matching each blow with an equal one.

clue.text: Manoeuvre robot right up quiet part of an aircraft

indicators.note: manoeuvre as a command means move these letters about into a new order

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A command to steer a robot quietly upward into the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvre' scrambles ROBOT, R, UP and P together; P is piano, quiet in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop is a gas-turbine engine driving a propeller, a component that powers some aircraft.

clue.text: Actress with ring to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for boast is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast
O is a ring shape

explanation.surface: A film star wearing a ring has something to show off about.
explanation.walkthrough: Greta Garbo, the Hollywood star; the reversed boast comes first though the ring is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Mistake brings doubly unappreciative response

indicators.note: doubly means the jeer is given twice in a row

parts.note: boo is the sound of a jeering crowd

explanation.surface: An error draws boos from a disappointed audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A booboo is informal slang for a silly blunder or error.

clue.text: Shame about character of Colin Dexter

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective created by the novelist Colin Dexter

explanation.surface: A reader feels ashamed regarding a fictional detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Colin Dexter wrote the Inspector Morse novels, set in Oxford and well known in Britain from television.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret and guilt for a wrong done, close to a feeling of shame.

clue.text: Female embarrassed with rip, which reveals contours

indicators.note: embarrassed signals that the words female and rip are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is red-faced about a tear in her clothes, showing her curves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' scrambles FEMALE and RIP; 'contours' tempts a reading about a figure, but it means lines of height on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows the shape of the land, with hills and valleys shown by contour lines or shading.

clue.text: Old American in error raised backing

indicators.note: in means the old American letters go inside the reversed error
raised in a down clue means the word for error is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: An elderly American who made an error is now held up as supportive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LAPSE upwards to ESPAL, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal is the adoption of or support for a cause, so it equates to backing.

clue.text: Sing high part

parts.note: to sing is slang for to inform on someone, as is to split
up means high, elevated

explanation.surface: Singers are told to take the top line in harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' and 'split' are both slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To split up is to separate or go different ways, which is to part.

clue.text: Such was hard for a princess, admitting hard, though tender once

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word for hard goes inside

parts.words: Such was hard for a princess
parts.note: in the fairy tale a princess felt a single pea through a stack of mattresses
set means hardened, as a jelly sets

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale princess complains of a hard bed, though she was tender.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale The Princess and the Pea, one pea under many mattresses bruised her. 'tender' means money, not sore.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency of Spain until the euro, so it was once legal tender.

clue.text: Sole from burn circling lake

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the word for burn wraps the lake letter

parts.note: to singe is to burn lightly

explanation.surface: A fish is fried near the water's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' tempts a fish, but it means only, one.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one and only, alone, which is a sense of sole.

clue.text: Staying power enlivens, pointless climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse
pointless means a compass point, here east, is dropped from the word

parts.note: animates means brings to life, enlivens

explanation.surface: Endurance brightens things up, though climbing seems futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' drops E (east, a compass point) from ANIMATES to give ANIMATS, and 'climbing' reads that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is physical or mental endurance, the capacity to keep going over a long effort.

clue.text: Believe it's too easy to get?

definitions.meaning: to believe a claim is to accept it as true
loans and borrowing on account are often said to be handed out too freely

explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to believe it, and credit is also borrowing that lenders give out loosely.

clue.text: Bird becomes parasite if back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the front letter of the word is moved to the back

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A bird turns into a pest when reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the first L of LOUSE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a thrush-like bird such as the blackbird or ring ousel.

clue.text: Jargon for tart with new filling

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the new letter sits within the word for tart

parts.note: slag is British ... for a promiscuous woman, as is tart

explanation.surface: A baker uses technical terms for a pastry with a fresh filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry, but it is a crude British word for a woman, as is SLAG; 'filling' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary peculiar to a group, much like jargon.

clue.text: Half that's not important?

definitions.meaning: a half is a half-pint glass of ale, a modest drink
something trivial and of no consequence

explanation.definitionFit: Small beer means trivial matters, and literally it is weak or small beer, such as a half-pint.

clue.text: Food from poor area in the country neither finished

indicators.note: in means the shortened poor area goes inside the shortened country
finished means the country's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Spain is a country

indicators.note: neither, with finished, means the poor area also loses its final letter

parts.note: a ghetto is a deprived district

explanation.surface: Meals come from a deprived district in a land where nothing is completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither finished' cuts the last letter from both the country and the poor area.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin pasta, a staple Italian food.

clue.text: One's unsettled, though sane?

parts.note: a wanderer with no fixed home, whose label split in two would say they are not crazy

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer reads as a claim of being not mad, which is sane.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad has no settled home, wandering from place to place.

clue.text: Bean to stick inside scallion briefly

indicators.note: inside means the word for stick goes within the shortened vegetable
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a leek is sometimes called a scallion
to gum is to stick, glue

explanation.surface: A cook glues a bean inside a chopped spring onion.
explanation.walkthrough: Scallion usually means a spring onion, but the word can also be used of a leek.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume is a pod-bearing plant, and a bean is one example of its seed.

clue.text: Flower container of prestige containing Italian flower

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the river goes inside the word for prestige

parts.note: cachet means prestige, distinction
the Po is Italy's longest river, something that flows, a flower

explanation.surface: A grand vase holds an Italian bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' twice tempts a bloom, but the second means something that flows, the river PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachepot is an ornamental holder for a potted plant, a container for flowers.
